1. THE SUPPLIED SPIN CERTIFICATE ALSO BOUNDS MINUS THE STAR

For diagonal weights w_i>=0 and the exact optimizer G from the supplied
spin theorem, write K=L+G and

  D=(3/5)K_A+(1/5)(K_B+K_C),
  W=sum_i w_i J_i^T tensor(J_i^B+J_i^C).

The supplied theorem proves D-W>=0. Its generic block structure proves
the additional operator inequality

  D+W>=0.                                                     (N2)

This is not inferred by substituting noncommuting variables or discarding
the sign. Here is the complete sign argument, on the same D2/BC-swap
block decomposition as the supplied certificate.

In each BC-symmetric parity-i sector, sign-flip the source's two y leaves
and order the five vectors as (x,yj,yk,uj,uk). The diagonal of 5(D-W) is
  (5Ki,3Ki+2Kj,3Ki+2Kk,Ki+4Kj,Ki+4Kk),
and all its nonzero off-diagonal entries are NONPOSITIVE:
  14=24=-5sqrt(2)wk; 15=35=-5sqrt(2)wj; 45=-5wi.
There is no diagonal W term. Reversing W keeps the diagonal and reverses
all these off-diagonal signs. For every complex vector v,

  v^dagger 5(D+W) v >= |v|^T 5(D-W) |v| >=0,                 (N3)

where |v| is the coordinatewise absolute value. The first inequality is
the triangle bound on each off-diagonal cross term; the second is exactly
the supplied PSD certificate. Thus the reversed five-dimensional blocks
are positive without regenerating polynomial optimizer certificates.

Each BC-antisymmetric parity block is two-dimensional. Its single
off-diagonal sign reversal is conjugation by diag(1,-1), so positivity
is unchanged. In the two all-odd three-dimensional blocks the diagonal
is identical, and their off-diagonal entries have opposite signs.
Reversing W exchanges these two blocks. Both were proved positive in
the supplied theorem. These eight blocks cover all 27 dimensions.
This proves (N2), including zero weights and all optimizer boundaries.

2. INDEPENDENT INPUT/RECEIVER ROTATIONS, INCLUDING ORIENTATION

Let U,V be real orthogonal 3x3 matrices. Define spin triads
J_i^R=sum_a V_(ai)J_a and J_i^L=sum_a U_(ai)J_a. For O orthogonal put
epsilon_O=det(O) and R_O=epsilon_O O, which is a proper rotation.
Then J(Oe_i)=epsilon_O R_O J_i R_O^T in the vector representation.
Consequently

  sum_i w_i (J_i^R)^T tensor(J_i^L,B+J_i^L,C)
